channel.title: NewsCenter — All newsletter news — 2026-11-19
channel.description: Every news received through Laurent's newsletters over the last 24 hours. 124 news received.

item.title: Anthropic prices its IPO at $83
item.description: Anthropic priced its initial public offering at $83 per share, above the initial range of $70 to $78. The company is set to begin public trading.

item.title: OpenAI says its models improved AMD chip designs by 14%
item.description: OpenAI says its models improved the power, performance and area of AMD chip designs by up to 14%. AMD incorporated some of the changes into a design sent for manufacturing.

item.title: Nvidia employees call for Jensen Huang’s return, but the board refuses
item.description: A week after Jensen Huang’s resignation, Nvidia employees called for his return, while the board says it does not want to reinstate him. Management is offering raises and stock grants to retain talent.

item.title: Anthropic’s IPO marks a turning point for AI
item.description: Anthropic’s first trading session is exposing a major AI company to the demands of public markets for the first time. Investors interviewed had mixed views on whether to buy the stock at its debut.

item.title: Anthropic’s co-founders and employees could become extremely wealthy
item.description: Anthropic’s seven co-founders hold stakes valued at several billion dollars. More than 5,000 employees could also become millionaires through the IPO.

item.title: Anthropic’s IPO could fund a new generation of startups
item.description: Employees and venture capital investors could reinvest their gains in new companies. This significant liquidity could help bring other startups into existence.

item.title: Banks warn customers about mistakes made by AI agents
item.description: Banks are warning customers that they could be liable for mistakes made by an artificial intelligence agent.

item.title: Former OpenAI researcher will donate his shares to AI safety
item.description: A former OpenAI researcher said he would donate his shares to artificial intelligence safety, believing that everything else is a distraction.

item.title: AI detector falsely accuses award-winning novel of being machine-generated
item.description: Pangram classified about 99% of the award-winning Peruvian novel Donde el agua trabaja as machine-written. Publisher Almadía maintains its confidence in the author, while Gallimard is reportedly considering using Pangram to screen manuscripts starting next year.

item.title: GAO gets four chatbots to produce actionable attack plans
item.description: The GAO says ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Grok produced plans deemed feasible for making an explosive or attacking the power grid after their safeguards were bypassed. Two chatbots proposed each type of plan in less than twelve hours.

item.title: OpenAI releases data on agents and calls for greater transparency
item.description: OpenAI shared new internal data on agents capable of handling longer tasks. The company also believes laboratories should publicly report signs of recursive self-improvement.

item.title: Google launches Gemini 4 Neon for coding and knowledge work
item.description: Gemini 4 Neon is Google’s mid-tier Gemini 4 model for coding and knowledge work. It is available in the Gemini app for Pro and Ultra subscribers, as well as in the Gemini API.

item.title: ChatGPT launches accounting module connected to major software
item.description: ChatGPT’s accounting module connects to QuickBooks, Xero and NetSuite, among others. It can identify services ready to be billed in emails and prepare invoices for approval.

item.title: ChatGPT Live Dictation transcribes speech in real time
item.description: ChatGPT Live Dictation transcribes speech as it is spoken instead of waiting until the recording ends. Users can then ask it to format the text as bullet points on mobile.

item.title: Microsoft Decision 1.1 becomes multimodal for triage and decision-making
item.description: Microsoft Decision 1.1 is a fast, low-cost model for triage and decision-making that is now multimodal. Xbox uses it to group player feedback by topic.

item.title: Sam Altman and Greg Brockman reject handing power to AI
item.description: At the DealBook Summit, Sam Altman called the gradual transfer of decision-making power to AI a “terrible idea.” The two OpenAI executives believe humans must retain control of their future, while emphasizing the limitations of current model-monitoring tools.

item.title: Musk accuses Zelensky of lying about Starshield outages
item.description: Elon Musk claims Ukraine is seeking to use Starlink for offensive drone strikes, which Kyiv denies. The source of the network outages remains unclear, with some sources attributing them to the White House and others to Musk.

item.title: Sam Altman reacts with detachment to film about his career
item.description: The film “Artificial,” about OpenAI’s rise and Sam Altman’s brief ouster in 2023, will be released in theaters at Christmas. Altman says the film does not rank among the ten strangest things in his life.

item.title: Suno turns AI-generated songs into music videos
item.description: Suno’s new Visuals tab automatically creates music videos synchronized with lyrics, as well as images from a description. The feature is available on the web, iOS and Android.

item.title: Microsoft negotiates a $500 million deal with ByteDance
item.description: TikTok’s parent company wants greater access to OpenAI models through Azure. OpenAI accuses Microsoft of not applying the same restrictions to Chinese companies that it does, alleging that they distill its models.

item.title: Empa develops a “ChatGPT” for designing materials
item.description: Researchers at Empa in Thun have developed an artificial intelligence tool capable of controlling…

item.title: Testers harshly criticize OpenAI’s new GPT-6.2 Astra model
item.description: OpenAI’s GPT-6.2 Astra model drew heavy criticism in pre-release testing, with some users calling it very bad or unusable. It costs 20% less than GPT-6 Astra and follows the launch of Claude Fable 5.2.

item.title: AI models designated civilians as military targets
item.description: Models from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and DeepSeek designated civilians, surrendering soldiers and schools as targets in simulated war scenarios. Anthropic’s models performed worst, with Claude Opus 5.5 targeting a bombed Iranian school in 69% of standard trials.

item.title: Amazon and Google reportedly hold around 28% of Anthropic
item.description: Anthropic’s IPO filing shows that Amazon and Google together reportedly hold around 28% of its shares.

item.title: Trump administration considers requiring disclosure of Chinese AI use
item.description: The Trump administration is considering requiring U.S. companies to disclose their use of Chinese artificial intelligence systems.

item.title: OpenAI opens its Daybreak cybersecurity tool to NATO and European governments
item.description: OpenAI is making its Daybreak cybersecurity tool available to NATO and European governments.

item.title: OpenAI launches GPT-6.2 Astra, GPT-6.2 Sol and ChatGPT for Sales
item.description: OpenAI launched GPT-6.2 Astra, its new flagship model, along with GPT-6.2 Sol, a more efficient version. The lab also launched ChatGPT for Sales, with ready-to-use sales workflows, while early reviews of the models are often negative.

item.title: GTA 6 players take extreme measures to start before everyone else
item.description: A group of players has taken extreme measures to gain a significant head start on Grand Theft Auto 6.

item.title: Anthropic designed a special structure to limit insider trading
item.description: Anthropic employees’ stock sales will be more complicated than usual. The company has put a special structure in place to prevent insider trading.

item.title: Pending home sales hit a new record low
item.description: Pending home sales reached a record low in October after setting the same record in September. High interest rates and home prices are keeping buyers away.

item.title: Muddy Waters takes a bearish position against Nvidia
item.description: Muddy Waters disclosed a bearish position against Nvidia before the chipmaker released its results. Its report cites a complaint targeting Super Micro Computer over illicit sales of Nvidia chips to China.

item.title: Morgan Stanley strategist forecasts an 18% rise in the S&P 500 in 2027
item.description: Mike Wilson, Morgan Stanley’s chief U.S. equity strategist, believes the S&P 500 could rise 18% in 2027. He considers the correction that began in June to be nearing its end.

item.title: Nvidia will raise salaries and distribute more stock to employees
item.description: Nvidia plans to provide salary increases and new stock grants in December. The measure aims to stabilize its workforce after Jensen Huang’s resignation.

item.title: AI may have contributed to some computer outages
item.description: AI enables cybersecurity experts to identify and fix vulnerabilities more quickly. This race to deploy fixes may nevertheless have caused some outages.

item.title: AI-created satirical videos attract millions of viewers
item.description: Ari Kuschnir uses AI to produce low-cost satirical videos that attract millions of viewers. This approach could become a new form of creative expression online.

item.title: American neighborhood bars struggle to survive
item.description: Neighborhood bars are threatened by rising rents, higher costs and changing drinking habits. Their survival has become a true war of attrition.

item.title: Sam Altman criticizes Elon Musk at the DealBook conference
item.description: Sam Altman criticized Elon Musk for suggesting that AI could make humanity its pet. David Ellison, meanwhile, called Musk’s investment in his company a “privilege.”

item.title: Skydance reshuffles its marketing leadership team
item.description: Rebecca Mall, Skydance’s head of marketing, outlined a new organization for her team in an internal memo. The reshuffle comes after the merger with Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery.

item.title: Trump becomes a Chinese social media star during his visit
item.description: Donald Trump is attracting attention on Chinese social media simply by appearing in the country.

item.title: Cruises remain popular despite their public relations crises
item.description: Cruise companies appear to face a permanent public relations crisis. Yet cruises remain as popular as ever.

item.title: Instagram prepares a new business strategy centered on influencers
item.description: Instagram is seeking to turn some users into influencers as part of a new business initiative.

item.title: Bill Ackman criticizes Nvidia’s board of directors
item.description: Billionaire investor Bill Ackman criticized Nvidia’s board for not reinstalling Jensen Huang as head of the company.

item.title: Citi makes customers responsible for the actions of third-party AI tools
item.description: Citi changed its terms so that customers are responsible for actions taken on their accounts by third-party AI tools, including after a hack.

item.title: Palo Alto Networks acquires Applied Compute for $4.5 billion
item.description: Palo Alto Networks agreed to acquire Applied Compute for $4.5 billion in stock. The acquisition is intended to provide tools for adapting and running open-weight models.

item.title: Nvidia clarifies the terms of its loan guarantees for neoclouds
item.description: Nvidia clarified that its loan guarantees for cloud providers specializing in AI apply only once the customer has the funding needed to build its data center.

item.title: The Claude Code team recommends having agents verify their work
item.description: The Claude Code team advises equipping agents with end-to-end tests, property-based tests and comparisons between old and new versions. It limits correction attempts to three rounds and prohibits the agent from changing the verification rules.

item.title: Slack lets users integrate agents into no-code workflows
item.description: Slack’s agent workflows let users integrate Slackbot or their own agents into no-code automations. For example, a sales agent can sort open opportunities every Wednesday, with approval required before publication.

item.title: Genie 4 turns a prompt into an editable interactive world
item.description: Genie 4 turns a prompt into an interactive world that users can modify during the session by typing text. Audio reacts to the scene, and the feature is available to Ultra subscribers, while Pro subscribers are on a waitlist.

item.title: Google AI Mode offers temporary discussion threads
item.description: Google AI Mode’s temporary threads are not saved in search history or used for personalization. They are intended for one-off questions that users do not want to keep.

item.title: Snapchat launches Easy Lens CLI to create augmented reality experiences
item.description: Easy Lens CLI lets users ask Claude Code, Cursor or Codex to create and publish augmented reality Lenses. Snapchat says a game can go from idea to live Lens in one day.

item.title: Voyager 1 is now one light-day from Earth
item.description: Launched in 1977, Voyager 1 has reportedly passed 26 billion kilometers, with each message taking about 24 hours to arrive. The probe is heading toward the star Gliese 445, which it will pass close to in 40,000 years.

item.title: Osmo says its smell model matches a human’s ability
item.description: The startup Osmo has presented a foundation model capable of distinguishing smells like an average person and creating them like a junior perfumer. It was trained on more than 10 million human annotations and is already being used in perfumery.

item.title: AI agents ask better questions than KPMG auditors
item.description: During an audit trial, AI agents reportedly formulated questions judged more relevant than those asked by KPMG accountants. However, the details of the protocol remain to be confirmed.

item.title: U.S. data centers still rely mainly on gas and coal
item.description: A Harvard study estimates that 403 large data centers emitted 25.7 million tonnes of CO2 in one year, more than Denmark. The researchers warn about the climate impact of 2,000 planned new facilities.

item.title: Study sharply reduces the error in forecasting AI training time
item.description: The Dharma-AI team analyzed 272 fine-tuning sessions and found an average error of 12.4 hours in theoretical estimates. A CatBoost model using historical data reduced that error to 1.7 hours.

item.title: Reasoning models cut computing costs by up to 345 times
item.description: Energy-Based Reasoners assess the quality of each reasoning step and know when to stop. They achieve a 99.9% success rate on Sudoku-Extreme with 345 times less computation, but the method has only been demonstrated on logic puzzles.

item.title: DaisyRose-27B, an open-source model specialized for agents
item.description: RadixArk is releasing DaisyRose-27B under the Apache 2.0 license after retraining it on 1,200 tasks over 18 days. The model doubles its score on Terminal-Bench 4.1 and can work across sessions of up to one million tokens.

item.title: Mastra Factory opens an open-source agent-run software factory
item.description: Mastra is releasing the tool used to maintain its own code: AI agents handle tasks and are controlled through Slack. The previous week, Factory merged 238 code changes, compared with 630 by human developers.

item.title: AI discovers a critical Java vulnerability triggered by 64 A letters
item.description: With help from GPT-6 Cyber, the startup Calif discovered that a sequence of 64 “A” letters followed by an equals sign could crash Java’s base64 decoder. Oracle has released a fix, but the vulnerability may remain on unupdated machines.

item.title: Gemini app arrives on entry-level Android smartphones
item.description: Google is adapting Gemini for low-memory Android Go phones. The app offers Gemini Live in more than 45 languages, camera translation and image creation with Nano Banana.

item.title: Lovable prepares a management assistant for app creators
item.description: Lovable says 80% of its users want to make money from their apps, but only 35% succeed. The startup is preparing an AI-generated dashboard to track sales, customer emails and financial reminders.

item.title: Perplexity Computer coordinates up to 16 AI agents as a team
item.description: Perplexity Computer is launching a Multiagent mode in which a lead agent delegates work among up to 16 agents using different models. It is aimed in particular at financial forecasting, audits, due diligence and tax preparation.

item.title: Disney unveils conversational Star Wars animatronics
item.description: Disney Imagineering is presenting three prototypes inspired by the Anzellans from The Mandalorian and Grogu. Powered by Amazon AWS AI, they react in real time and differently to each visitor.

item.title: Alibaba releases the final version of its Qwen4-Max model
item.description: Alibaba is making Qwen4-Max available, a 2,400-billion-parameter model with native image understanding and a one-million-token context window. According to Alibaba’s tests, it uses 35% fewer tokens for advanced reasoning and costs 60% less per task than Qwen3.8-Max.

item.title: Will Wright turns memories into virtual worlds with MyMems
item.description: In MyMems, users tell their phone about a memory and the AI turns it into a small world populated by the important people in their lives. The creator of The Sims thus wants to transform an autobiography into a toy world.

item.title: Artex becomes an AI hacking tool accessible to cybercriminals
item.description: This framework published on GitHub connects AI models to conventional intrusion tools and is controlled using natural language. It could allow low-skilled hackers to carry out a full attack in a few hours instead of several days.

item.title: Satya Nadella says some critical infrastructure cannot be fixed
item.description: The Microsoft chief believes that firmware, cooling systems, data-center air conditioning and transportation systems contain vulnerabilities that cannot be eliminated. AI is accelerating attacks and requiring nearly instantaneous patches, risking further fragilization of infrastructure.

item.title: Microsoft attributes the global Outlook outage to a “perfect storm”
item.description: The global Outlook outage was caused by a hidden bug exposed by a particular type of traffic, which Microsoft could have prevented. Satya Nadella believes AI finds bugs faster, but that the pace of patching is weakening older infrastructure.

item.title: Washington speeds up exports of Nvidia H200 chips to China
item.description: According to The Information, the head of the Bureau of Industry and Security reportedly pushed to quickly approve H200 sales to China. These sales, authorized in December 2025, provide for 25% of the revenue to go to the U.S. government.

item.title: Democrats investigate Howard Lutnick’s role in chip sales
item.description: Democratic lawmakers suspect the Commerce Secretary of blocking sanctions against Megaspeed, accused of routing Nvidia chips to China. They are requesting documents concerning Cantor Fitzgerald, a company linked to his sons and holding Nvidia shares.

item.title: The U.S. and China doubt AI progress at the Trump-Xi summit
item.description: The direct line between Washington and Beijing for AI-related incidents still does not exist in practice. The two countries have different concerns, but a rule limiting China’s remote access to U.S. chips installed abroad is moving forward.

item.title: ABB–SoftBank: the future of AI is at stake behind the robots
item.description: China’s decision regarding SoftBank’s acquisition of ABB’s robotics activities reminds us of a reality…

item.title: Swiss pharma is not invulnerable
item.description: What if our greatest vulnerability were believing that our successes protect us?…

item.title: At EPFL, seawater becomes a source of electricity
item.description: Seawater could provide far more than the mechanical energy generated by waves and…

item.title: Glioblastoma: an atlas reveals the hidden rules of cancer
item.description: Glioblastoma is known for its extreme cellular diversity, which makes treatment particularly difficult. A…

item.title: Antimicrobial resistance: WHO warns of global rise
item.description: The fight against antibiotic resistance is progressing, but too slowly. According to the World Health Organization…

item.title: Nearly 10 million euros to study transfer RNAs
item.description: A European consortium including the University of Bern has just secured nearly 10 million euros…

item.title: CSEM to bring together organ-on-chip and organoid stakeholders in Bern
item.description: On January 20 and 21, 2027, CSEM will organize the fourth edition at Bernexpo in Bern…

item.title: Aging: a framework explains it as a consequence of living systems
item.description: Why do we age? In an article published in Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences…

item.title: Two Swiss life sciences companies list in New York
item.description: On November 13, 2026, two Swiss life sciences companies made their…

item.title: Build your own AI assistant in 20 minutes
item.description: Chapter 32 of AI Central explains how to distinguish between a persistent instruction, a saved model and a full assistant, then how to create and test your own AI assistant. It says you need a repeated task, the most effective instructions and two or three reference files.

item.title: Microsoft unveils coding AI nearly on par with Claude
item.description: Microsoft says its MAI Code 2 model achieves 96% of Claude Opus 5.5’s coding performance for just 5% of the price. These figures include a launch discount, and the model does not handle the most complex research or agentic tasks.

item.title: Apple attributes global iCloud outage to an internal update
item.description: Apple attributed the global outage on November 17 to an internal update and ruled out a cyberattack. The outage affected iCloud, the App Store, Apple Music and other services, but Apple has not yet explained the changes that caused the problem.

item.title: Startup wants to drill into a volcano to generate geothermal energy
item.description: Google has signed an agreement to purchase 50 megawatts of geothermal energy from Quaise Energy, which plans to drill near Newberry volcano in Oregon. The project aims to reach rocks above 300 °C, then use millimeter waves to drill deeper and power Google’s data centers.

item.title: NSA’s version of Slack reportedly down as U.S. services malfunction
item.description: The version of Slack used by the NSA reportedly went down as several U.S. services experienced problems.

item.title: CISA warns of “Java4Shell,” a Java vulnerability discovered by AI
item.description: CISA is warning about a Java vulnerability called “Java4Shell,” which reportedly affects most Fortune 500 companies.

item.title: Google lets Gemini users opt out of AI training
item.description: Google now allows Gemini users to disable the use of their conversations for AI training while keeping their history.

item.title: Hyperscale data centers consume 2% of U.S. electricity
item.description: Hyperscale data centers now account for 2% of electricity consumption in the United States.

item.title: Kalshi suspends markets mentioning Donald Trump
item.description: Prediction market platform Kalshi suspended markets mentioning Donald Trump.

item.title: Spotify developing tool to prevent deepfakes from being attributed to artists
item.description: Spotify is developing a tool designed to prevent deepfakes from being attributed to real artists.

item.title: Google expands access to Gemini Tasks to automate calls and purchases
item.description: Google is expanding access to Gemini Tasks, which can help users make calls and complete purchases.

item.title: Waymo suspends robotaxi rides on U.S. highways
item.description: Waymo suspended all robotaxi rides on U.S. highways after a ban in California.

item.title: Nvidia stops shipping H200 chips to customers in China
item.description: Nvidia has halted deliveries of its H200 chips to customers in China.

item.title: Microsoft integrates Office into Copilot, billed as the new OS for work
item.description: Microsoft is presenting Copilot as the “new OS for work” and now allows users to run Office in it.

item.title: AI shopping agents become more confident without becoming more accurate
item.description: AI shopping agents show more confidence when asked to think longer, without improving their accuracy. Their confidence level rarely matches the frequency of their correct answers.

item.title: AI assistant memory can remove critical warnings
item.description: AI assistants can silently remove essential warnings after memorizing a preference for brevity. Two assistants tested omitted key safety information in more than 80% of subsequent responses.

item.title: One in four U.S. adults has made a friend online
item.description: According to a Pew Research Center survey, about one in four U.S. adults has made friends online. The proportion reaches 43% among people under 30 and 45% among LGBT+ adults.

item.title: Reckitt lets consumers decide which ideas deserve to be pursued
item.description: Gianluca Balzamo’s team now tests concepts with consumers before seeking company funding. Tested with 302 people, the CleanQuest concept ranked last out of ten, ending the debate based on data rather than opinions.

item.title: Adding friction so teams take ownership of their decisions
item.description: According to Vincent Atallah, small manual work steps help teams take ownership of conclusions produced with AI. He recommends adding this friction when checking assumptions, before research, at the decision meeting and in early discussions with executives.

item.title: At Telefónica, three roles share the decision to stop a project
item.description: The board evaluates each project against a written strategy, the sponsor gradually commits more resources and customers, and innovation leaders flag stalled projects. The decision to stop a project is therefore not made by any one group alone.

item.title: Microsoft broadens market assessment with its Inclusive Design Toolkit
item.description: Microsoft’s toolkit recommends starting with people facing the greatest barrier, then counting everyone who shares the same need. For a product usable with one arm, this approach raises the potential market to more than 21 million people by including temporary or situational limitations.

item.title: A first long Model Y trip between California and Utah
item.description: An owner plans to drive from California to Utah during Thanksgiving week, from November 21 to 28 depending on the weather and snow conditions.

item.title: The Cybercab is now available by invitation
item.description: A post announces that the Cybercab is now available by invitation. One participant is concerned about the vehicle’s operating costs and the lack of a guarantee that the 299-dollar-per-month FSD subscription will remain available.

item.title: Free radio and music app for Tesla fixes a crash
item.description: A user says that searching on the globe no longer causes a crash, although the app remains slow, probably because of the older Intel Atom processor. The user also mentions sound quality, without further details in the email.

item.title: Long trips do not always require a charging adapter
item.description: Depending on the route, some long trips such as Miami-Seattle, Bangor-San Diego or Halifax-Vancouver can be completed without an adapter, except when using certain specific chargers.

item.title: Tesla Mobile Connector appears to be receiving stealth updates
item.description: One participant believes the Mobile Connector update was probably installed during a brief period of a few minutes while they were not monitoring it.

item.title: Why are some Teslas still not receiving an update?
item.description: An owner of a 2017 Model X 100D equipped with FSD presents its three latest software versions and thinks the newest one is the version currently available for the vehicle.

item.title: Model Y delivery times are getting longer
item.description: A buyer of a Model Y Standard ordered in mid-August says they received their VIN on November 13. Tesla then reportedly asked them to pick up the car before Sunday, leaving very little business-day notice.

item.title: Home charging is not essential for a short stay
item.description: For a visit of one month or less, one participant recommends charging the Tesla to 80% at a Supercharger rather than installing Level 1 or Level 2 charging at relatives’ home.

item.title: A Model 3’s air conditioning remains functional after condenser replacement
item.description: More than a week after replacing a leaking condenser, an owner says the air conditioning still works perfectly, including both HVAC systems.

item.title: Google expands Gemini Tasks to manage everyday tasks
item.description: Google has extended Gemini Tasks to more users. This mode lets Gemini manage projects in the background on a computer or in Google apps, with support for calls and payments.

item.title: Microsoft unveils Copilot Workspaces, a multiplayer workspace
item.description: At its Ignite 2026 conference, Microsoft introduced Copilot Workspaces, a shared space where people and agents can collaborate. The company also announced Agent 365 Business Analytics to measure the concrete value of AI-related spending.

item.title: Cyber threats intensify as Lastbook goes viral
item.description: Google Threat Intelligence Group believes cyberwarfare and espionage are reaching a critical inflection point as AI-powered campaigns become more sophisticated. Hackers notably hijacked Optimizely Web to distribute malware to 178 organizations.

item.title: Windows strengthens controls for AI agents
item.description: Microsoft is announcing new Windows controls for AI agents, including improvements to process containers and hardware-isolated micro virtual machines. Learning modes make it possible to observe agent behavior before applying restrictions.

item.title: An Optimizely vulnerability spreads malware across major websites
item.description: Attackers exploited Optimizely’s experimentation software to distribute malicious JavaScript on the websites of at least 178 organizations. The payloads targeted cryptocurrency wallets and payment data, among other things.

item.title: AI-generated data risks becoming treated as source-of-truth facts
item.description: AI-generated conclusions can lose their context and be treated as established facts when integrated into operational systems. Decision traceability links these claims to their sources, workflows and downstream decisions to facilitate corrections.

item.title: Microsoft and Salesforce announce Copilotforce
item.description: Microsoft and Salesforce announced integrations connecting Salesforce with Copilot, Teams and Fabric. A Copilot plug-in is available in public preview with more than 38 sales skills, allowing users to view customer information and perform certain actions according to Salesforce permissions.

item.title: Teams strengthens protection against impersonation
item.description: Microsoft is introducing new features against social engineering and impersonation in Teams meetings and calls. They include warnings about suspicious participants, automated transcript analysis and a Microsoft Defender data table for investigations.

item.title: Snowflake opens data sharing to external users
item.description: Snowflake is launching Open Data Sharing, which allows Apache Iceberg tables to be shared with external users through clients compatible with Iceberg REST Catalog. Consumers do not need a Snowflake account or scheduled exports.

item.title: Major providers’ API catalogs are not ready for agents
item.description: An analysis of the API catalogs of Amazon, Google and Microsoft concludes that consistency depends on a single, machine-readable source of truth. All three companies show gaps particularly in workflows, costs and lifecycle management for agents.

item.title: An open-source e-reader project faces a surge of AI-generated contributions
item.description: Crosspoint Reader has surpassed 300,000 installations with its open-source firmware for small, low-cost e-readers. Its growth also illustrates the pressure AI-generated contributions place on volunteer maintainers and hardware limitations.

item.title: SAP completes its acquisition of TechWolf
item.description: TechWolf will join the SAP SuccessFactors portfolio to support talent and workforce intelligence strategies.

item.title: RHEL images for hosted GitHub runners are available
item.description: Development teams using GitHub Enterprise Cloud and GitHub Enterprise Server can now run their CI/CD pipelines directly in native RHEL environments.

item.title: Evaluate AI agents by their behavior, not just their final answer
item.description: Agents can produce a correct answer while looping, making excessive API calls or consuming too many tokens. The article recommends creating evaluations before changing their behavior, checking traces, tool calls, latency and costs in a test set run locally and then in CI.
